title: Exact restriction from semilinear systems to constant towers
statement: Let $R_n$ be commutative rings with maps $c_n:R_{n+1}\to R_n$, let $B$ be a commutative ring and let $\psi_n:B\to R_n$ satisfy $c_n\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n$. Use the actual module-system categories of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] and strict constant towers of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. There exists an additive exact functor from each module-system category to the corresponding strict $B$-tower category whose level functors are evaluation followed by restriction along $\psi_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The level identifications are identity on every section, and the tower transitions are the original horizontal section restrictions. Identity on sections is expressed pointwise: for every input section x, its image under the level identification is heterogeneously equal to x.

proof.text: For each n compose evaluation with restriction along the constant-sheaf map induced by psi_n, using [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. The compatibility c_n psi_(n+1) = psi_n and the restriction-composition identity identify the twice-restricted n-th level with directly restricted coefficients. Whisker the existing horizontal transition with scalar restriction and this identification. Functor.ofOpSequence turns these adjacent natural transformations into a tower-valued functor. The restriction-composition identification is identity on sections, so transition_exists supplies the exact transition formula. Each level is evaluation followed by restriction, giving the identity-on-sections level iso. The constructed level iso is the identity, so its pointwise heterogeneous section equation is HEq.rfl. The private transition section lemma applies the scalar-composition section equation directly to an input section and then the existing transition formula; the tower transition proof uses that pointwise equation.

On morphisms the constructed functor retains the original section maps; hence addition is preserved. Evaluation and scalar restriction preserve finite limits and colimits by evaluationLimits/evaluationColimits and resLimits/resColimits of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. The level iso transfers those properties to each tower evaluation; finite limits and colimits in a functor category are componentwise.
